claims.text: Opus 5 launched at $5/Mtok input and $25/Mtok output — identical to Opus 4.8 — with an optional fast mode at roughly 2.5x default speed for double the price ($10/$50)
Zhipu's GLM-5.2 ... landing close to Opus 4.8 on a handful of specific coding benchmarks, even as third-party comparisons show double-digit-point gaps favoring Opus 4.8 on several others

Per a company spokesperson quoted by VentureBeat, the pitch is explicitly three-tiered ... Mythos 5 ... described by a secondary pricing-tracker source as withheld because it is unusually good at finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities, a characterization this research could not confirm
Frontier-Bench v0.1 scores peak at xhigh — 44.4% — and dip to 43.3% at the top level, max, independently reproduced by Artificial Analysis's own Coding Agent Index
Multiple outlets relaying Anthropic's launch chart report the identical shape, but the stronger confirmation is that Artificial Analysis independently re-ran its own Coding Agent Index
CodeRabbit ... found the effort dial behaves ... Standard 35.2% precision / 61.1% recall; x-high 39.3% precision / 55.2% recall
CodeRabbit's own conclusion ... "effort was a routing decision... nothing improved uniformly"
FrontierCode is Cognition's own proprietary 150-task, 36-repo coding benchmark (with a 50-task "Diamond" hard subset), not an Epoch AI product
a Cognition team member conceded they would need roughly 50+ runs per model for real statistical confidence but had only run about five
a single evaluator's tweet with no raw numbers published, later amplified into commentary that repeats the tweet without independently verifying it
arXiv:2507.14417, "Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute" — documenting Claude reasoning models becoming more distracted by irrelevant context the longer they reason
Opus 5 (ECI) 159 (CI 157-162); Fable 5 (ECI) 161; SWE-ECI Opus 5 = Fable 5 = 161
a DeepSeek-R1-Distill checkpoint on GSM-8K climbs from 82.2% at 385 tokens to a peak of 87.3% at 1,100 tokens, then falls a full 17 points to 70.3% at 15,980 tokens
Gemini 2.5 Pro ... peaks at its smallest tested token budget (128 tokens, 90% accuracy) and never beats that figure ... Gemini 2.5 Flash tracing a milder version (92%→93%→92%)
GPT-5 Thinking's score nearly doubles from low to medium reasoning effort (7.903 → 15.336), but pushing to high effort ... actively drops the score to 12.626

Gemini 2.5 Pro's cheapest "minimal thinking" setting scores highest at 32.35%; effort has to pass through a worse "low" tier (28.43%) before partially recovering to a still-below-baseline 30.88% at "ultrathink"

the checks also review everything the model reads, not just your latest message ... memory, connector output, web search results, and attached files can all trip the classifier; biology/chemistry gets no fallback; consumer surfaces show a notice and sticky model switch

Automatic switching isn't active by default ... via the anthropic-beta: server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 header plus a fallbacks: "default" request parameter. Without that opt-in ... it returns a plain HTTP 200 with stop_reason: "refusal"
A GitHub issue against the third-party tool oh-my-pi shows the fallback signal present in three separate places in the API response — the client simply never parsed any of them
Developer Jonathon Ready reacted within hours, framing the clause as proof that "Claude can now be silently nerfed" ... a "supply chain risk"
fast.ai's Jeremy Howard among those widely quoted across press coverage of the incident: "They've said they'll sabotage others who try [to build competing frontier LLMs]"

three overlapping causes ... a reasoning-effort default downgrade (Mar 4-Apr 7), a caching bug (shipped Mar 26), and a verbosity-limiting system-prompt change (added Apr 16) ... all remediated by April 20 ... "never intentionally degrade[s]" its models

Anthropic quotes Niko Grupen ... Opus 5 matches Opus 4.8's max-reasoning performance while generating 26% fewer tokens on average ... adding an 11.7% all-pass score on Harvey's proprietary Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB)
Harvey's own scale ... an $11B valuation, roughly $190M in ARR, and about 1,300 client organizations as of a March 2026 raise reported by CNBC
on Zapier's own public leaderboard, Opus 5's best overall pass rate was only around 26% at launch ... the leaderboard score behind the marketing quote runs on a private, undisclosed held-out set
The company (formerly Altera, maker of the Excel-based finance agent "Shortcut") raised a $33M Series A led by Prosus on top of roughly $40M total funding
METR's most recent published Anthropic review covers Opus 4.6, dated roughly four and a half months before Opus 5 shipped

Independent commentator Zvi Mowshowitz surfaced pushback on the framing in his own review of the system card, quoting another commentator's sharper category-error framing ... approvingly, while describing his own reaction to the phrase as one of visible discomfort

Anthropic's disclosed annualized revenue run-rate went from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025 to an intermediate ~$30 billion ... 80x growth ... with later press coverage placing the run-rate at approximately $47 billion by May 2026
a $965 billion primary Series H round closed around May 28, 2026, with secondary-market marks reportedly reaching as high as $1.2 trillion by July 9, 2026
Claude Code ... went from about $500 million in annualized run-rate revenue in September 2025 to roughly $8 billion by May 2026
The EU AI Act's Article 13 covers only "predetermined" performance changes, and its "substantial modification" concept has never been tested against a mid-session model-substitution scenario
the sitting SEC Chair has explicitly said the agency "should resist the temptation to adopt prescriptive disclosure requirements for every 'new thing'"
One commentator frames the resulting gray zone sharply: "the model ID has quietly become a legal identifier"
